原聲低音吉他可見於墨西哥傳統音樂與瑪麗亞奇樂團，例如大型深身的guitarrón: The acoustic bass guitar appears in Mexican traditional music and mariachi, as the large, deep-bodied guitarrón, the plectrum-played león and the twelve-string six-course bajo sexto; the bajoloche style is played by slapping or plucking. From the 1970s it entered folk and rock settings as well: the folk musician Ashley Hutchings used one in his band, and Mike Oldfield used one on the 1975 album Ommadawn; the television programme Unplugged also made it the bass choice for unplugged line-ups. A resonator bass guitar is played by Les Claypool of Primus.
原聲低音吉他是一種空心木製琴身的弦鳴樂器，霍恩博斯特尔–薩克斯編號321.322: The acoustic bass guitar is a chordophone with a hollow wooden body, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322, usually larger than a steel-string acoustic guitar. Like the conventional electric bass and the double bass it is a bass instrument, usually with four strings, sounding an octave below the lowest four strings of a six-string guitar. It is played with the fingers or a pick; in Mexican traditional music it appears in mariachi and similar settings, and in the later twentieth century it was used in acoustic performance, folk and rock music.

原聲低音吉他通常為四弦，定音E-A-D-G，比六弦吉他最低四弦低一個八度。其空心: The acoustic bass guitar usually has four strings tuned E-A-D-G, an octave below the lowest four strings of a six-string guitar. Its hollow wooden body is mostly larger than a steel-string guitar's, so the low resonance is fuller, and the early large, deep-bodied designs in particular increase the bass volume. Even so, in ensemble with other acoustic instruments it may be hard to hear without amplification, so most instruments carry a magnetic or piezo pickup, with the volume set at a bass amplifier. Compared with the electric bass it is closer to the tone of an acoustic guitar; compared with the double bass, some semi-acoustic models or synthetic pickups can imitate its sound, but the body remains guitar-shaped.
墨西哥傳統音樂已有吉他式低音樂器，如馬里亞奇樂團使用的guitarrón；Ern: Mexican traditional music already had guitar-shaped bass instruments such as the guitarrón used in mariachi; Ernie Ball went to Tijuana to buy one and modify it. In 1972 he and the former Fender employee George William Fullerton brought out a large acoustic bass guitar with a deep body and more bass volume. In the late 1980s the television Unplugged programmes made it more common, and the Washburn model became the bass players' first choice. In 1974 and 1975 Ashley Hutchings used one with the Etchingham Steam Band; Mike Oldfield had one made by Tony Zemaitis in the mid-1970s and used it on recordings, including Ommadawn in 1975.

A beginner should get to know the tuning and the plucking first, and with a five-string or a low B string should watch for the body resonating too little, relying on the pickup and a bass amplifier to amplify if need be.
